# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

Every rule could be settled from the code. The basics (robots.txt, crawler access, links) are in place. Points are lost on a missing `lang`, a missing `Sitemap:` line, a noindexed Pricing page, and a Blog page that loads its content in the browser only. These results are read from code. No live site was checked.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Add a language to the page
- **Why it matters:** The `lang` attribute tells search engines and AI tools which language the site is written in. Without it, every page lacks this signal (GEO-012).
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11`
- **What the code says:** `<html>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 80 (80–80)

### 2. Point robots.txt at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** You have a sitemap, but robots.txt doesn't mention it. Crawlers that read robots.txt first won't be told where it is (GEO-011).
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` (the file has no `Sitemap:` line). Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 18.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 80 (80–80)

### 3. Let Pricing be indexed, or remove it from the sitemap
- **Why it matters:** Pricing is in your nav and sitemap, and it has a canonical (the page's preferred address). But it also tells search engines not to index it. These signals contradict each other, and a main page is hidden (GEO-014, GEO-015). If this is deliberate, drop it from the sitemap and nav instead, and tell me.
- **Where:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 18.25 ÷ 23 × 100 = 79 (79–79)

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Clear | `*` allows `/`. Only GPTBot (training) is blocked, which matches your policy |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` noindex. 3 of 4 routes clear (/, /docs, /blog) |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical to an indexable URL | Problem | `/` clear. `/pricing` canonical points to a noindex page. `/docs` and `/blog` have no canonical, so they aren't counted |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in server HTML | Problem | `app/blog/page.tsx:8` fetches in `useEffect`. 3 of 4 routes clear |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Searched the repo for `ld+json` and `@type`. None found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line. The sitemap file itself is valid |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | `app/layout.tsx:11` has no `lang`. Titles and descriptions are present on all pages |
| GEO-016 | Key pages reachable through real links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:13` uses `<a href>` to all four main pages |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't block AI search | Clear | Only element-scoped `data-nosnippet` (`app/layout.tsx:15`) |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Read the layout and 5 pages. No images, and links and buttons have text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app profile declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (informational) | Not scored | Not present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (informational) | Not scored | Not an app |

## Other problems found

- **A noindex page is in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:4`: `<loc>https://www.ledger.example/pricing</loc>`. Pricing is noindexed, so either remove it from the sitemap or remove the noindex (see item 3).
- **The sitemap has no `<lastmod>` dates.** This is not a defect, so see "Worth considering".

## Worth considering

- **Make the Blog render on the server:** `app/blog/page.tsx:8`: `fetch('/api/posts')`. Fetch the posts in a Server Component, with no `'use client'`. Then the titles are in the HTML crawlers receive. Also give each post its own page and address, because each article is currently only a title with no link.
- **Add canonicals to Docs and Blog:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` has only a title and description. Set `alternates: { canonical: '/docs' }`. `metadataBase` is already set in the layout, so it resolves to an absolute URL. Do the same for `/blog`.
- **Label the site's identity:** `app/layout.tsx:5` has the name "Ledger". Add Organization and WebSite JSON-LD with the name and URL, so machines can read who the site is from.
- **Flesh out Docs:** `app/docs/page.tsx:4`: `Start by importing your bank feed.` The page promises setup help but has one sentence. Add the actual steps as text.
- **Back up the Pricing claim:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:4`: `Free for up to three people.` The page title says "Plans for every team size", but only one plan appears. List the plans and prices as text, and consider Product or Offer structured data.
- **Say more on the home page:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Invoices, expenses and reports in one place.` Link onward to Pricing and Docs from the page body, and describe what each feature does.
- **Make titles say more:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Docs'` and `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Pricing'`. Use "Ledger Docs: set up your accounting" and similar, so search results show whose page it is.
- **Add `<lastmod>`:** `public/sitemap.xml:3` has no dates. Add real last-modified dates, or generate the sitemap with `app/sitemap.ts`.
- **Add a viewport tag:** `app/layout.tsx:3` metadata has no social tags (`openGraph`). Add them so shared links show a proper title and description.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status of robots.txt and sitemap URLs (live only):** the files are in `public/`, so they should be served, but a live check would confirm it.
- **`/api/posts`:** no route file for it exists in the repo, so I can't see where the Blog data comes from.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- I read all 5 routes (`/`, `/pricing`, `/docs`, `/blog`, `/thank-you`), the layout and nav, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and `geo.config.json`. I searched for JSON-LD and found none. `/thank-you` isn't linked or listed, so I left it out of the route counts. Its noindex looks deliberate.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
